description: ODC: SERVICE ACTION. Mirrors tests/jobs/service-action.json and tests/jobs/service-action-update.json and answers the question that the two jobs of the O11 lane leave unanswered: who calls a service action? THIS JOB WAS REWRITTEN TO BE A PROOF AND NOT A NARRATIVE. A checker caught it creating objects and telling the story in get/dump/usages -- reads that Anvil prints in the result but that NO gate reads. Each claim below now says WHICH gate kills it if it is false, and the ones that no gate can kill are named as such, without pretending to be proof. There are three gates available: (a) path resolution -- a get on a path that does not exist makes the op fail and the job returns ok=False; (b) the data contract, which since today also watches NAMED TOP-LEVEL ELEMENTS and the IServiceAction is one of them, so Description/Public/Shareable written here are read back at the end and a divergence gives 'Data property mismatch'; (c) the message contract, with expectedMessages: a new undeclared message gives unexpected, and a declared one that does not appear gives missingExpected. THE CORE OF THE JOB is an experiment with a control, and not a sentence: WfSvcOrder_ControlNoConsumer is a PRIVATE SERVER action with no consumer and its UnusedUserAction is declared -- if ODC stopped giving it, the job fails with missingExpected; the two SERVICE actions are equally at zero consumers (usages=0) and expectedMessages has no entry at all for them -- if either of them received UnusedUserAction, the job fails with unexpected. Both sides of the contrast are fatal, measured in the same run and on the same base. And the contrast is what explains the rest: the consumer of a service action is REMOTE (it arrives as ReferenceServiceAPIMethod, which Anvil reads as IServiceActionSignature), so 'no local consumer' is not 'unused'. The product itself says so at birth: an IServiceAction is born with ONE child, an ICommentNode written by OutSystems ('Service Actions run logic in a loosely coupled manner: - In a separate transaction. - Remotely in the producer context. - Changes are immediately available to all consumers upon publishing.'); that birth is now gate (a) on one side -- get on $svc/#ICommentNode -- and remains the deletion of a child that has to exist on the other. The LOCAL call does not exist and this was MEASURED, not assumed: an IExecuteServerActionNode with Action pointing to an IServiceAction is refused by the ODC Model API with 'A OutSystems.Model.Logic.IServiceAction cannot be used as the value for the OutSystems.Model.Logic.Nodes.IExecuteServerActionNode.Action property in a OutSystems.Model.Logic.IServerAction'. That refusal does NOT fit inside this file: a green job cannot contain an op that fails, and the only place where it becomes proof is a tests/jobs-odc-negative job with expectError, which this job does not create. It is recorded here as a measurement with the exact message, not as proof of the suite. The call that EXISTS is the one from inside out and that is a double gate: the public service action delegates to WfSvcOrder_Summarize, a PRIVATE server action with an aggregate (join to a static entity), if and assign -- if the Action set did not settle, the Verify would fail AND the Summarize would leave WfSvcOrder_Summarize at zero consumers, which would give it an undeclared UnusedUserAction. Two halves as in the O11 lane: WfSvcOrder_GetSummary through the raw verbs, WfSvcOrder_MarkPaid through the compact language with kind 'service' -- and that this really gives a ServiceAPIMethod is also gate (a), because three ops of this job address it by 'IServiceAction:WfSvcOrder_MarkPaid' and that path would not resolve on a server action. THIRD ACT (edit and delete what is already built and connected): the swapped description is read back by gate (b); the leftover input is deleted and that is gate (c), because leaving it there gives 'Input Parameter RequestedBy is never used in Service Action WfSvcOrder_GetSummary' (UnusedElement, measured); the renamed output is gate (a) in BOTH directions -- the get of $svc/OrderSummary only resolves if the rename settled, and the get of $sum/Summary only resolves if the rename did NOT drag along the homonymous output of the server action, which is the lesson that rename follows the key and not the text. And the property that SS11 does not have: Shareable. Public and Shareable are COUPLED, and here is the HONEST LIMIT of this job: the data contract knows how to compare what the job WROTE, it does not know how to assert a value that the job did NOT write. The four states of the pair in WfSvcOrder_GetSummary remain reads without a gate, and the reason lies in the arithmetic of the contract itself: if the job ended in a state produced by the drag, the contract would fail it as a divergence from the last write -- that is, with today's verbs the coupling can only be shown as a FAILURE, never as green proof. What this job can pin down is something else, and it pins it down: WfSvcOrder_MarkPaid ends up PRIVATE, on purpose. The birth state is Public=True/Shareable=True, so a job that ends in that state cannot tell 'I wrote' from 'I never touched'; ending in Public=False, gate (b) now requires that the write settled on a value that birth did not give. For the coupling to stop being narrative, one verb is missing from the kernel, named at the end of this job.

expectedMessages.why: It is the CONTROL of this job's experiment, and not dead code left by oversight: a private server action at zero consumers MUST receive UnusedUserAction in ODC, and the two service actions at zero consumers CANNOT receive anything. Declaring this one and leaving the others undeclared makes the contrast fatal on both sides -- without it, the sentence 'the service action does not get UnusedUserAction' was a claim about a message that nobody forced to exist elsewhere.

structures.name: WfSvcSummary
structures.description: O contrato que atravessa para fora: texto e numeros, sem identificadores da entidade. E por isto que uma service action devolve uma structure e nao a entidade -- o consumidor remoto nao fica preso ao modelo de dados do produtor

ops.name: WfSvcOrder_Summarize
ops._why: FIRST the internal logic, in a PRIVATE server action. It is the pair the platform asks for: the service action is the public door and stays thin; the one that knows how to read the database is this one. The aggregate with a join to a static entity is the same as in tests/jobs/service-action.json
the second source is the STATIC entity: the Label comes from it, the text that the contract promises
cita o parametro da action: nasce um IImplicitParameter dentro do aggregate
INSIDE the logic the aggregate line comes with the entity wrapper (.Current.WfSvcOrder.X), because an aggregate can join several sources -- and this one does
the other side of the join: the Label of the static entity becomes the text of the contract

ops.name: WfSvcOrder_GetSummary
ops._why: THE MISSING ARTIFACT. It is born in @espace as a server action, but in the ServiceActions collection and with the descriptor ServiceStudio.Model.Flows+ServiceAPIMethod

THE BIRTH, and it is now a GATE and not a read: a service action is not born empty nor with Start/End (the IRestServiceAction is born with terminals, this one is not), it is born with ONE ICommentNode written by OutSystems. This get addresses that child by type; if the platform stopped creating it, the path would not resolve and the job would return ok=False. The dump that follows is the read, and it serves to put the text in the result: 'In a separate transaction', 'Remotely in the producer context'. The TEXT itself has no gate -- see the kernel note at the end of the job
the same birth seen from above, so that the result keeps the only child and the text that OutSystems puts there
the other side of the birth: Public=True and Shareable=True ALREADY come on (an IServerAction is born private), CollectionDescriptor=ServiceActions and Nodes=1 -- that comment

ops.value: Resumo de uma encomenda para consumidores remotos

ops.name: RequestedBy
ops._why: this one comes in now and GOES OUT in the third act: it is the input left over from a contract, the case that the ODC lane had never deleted

ops.name: WfSvcOrderNotFound
ops._why: the exception that crosses to the remote consumer. PLATFORM DIFFERENCE recorded: in ODC the IUserException has no Description -- only CreatedBy, LastModifiedBy, LastModifiedDate and Name are writable

ops.name: Summarize
ops._why: THE CALL THAT EXISTS: from inside a service action to a server action. The reverse -- an IExecuteServerActionNode pointing to the IServiceAction -- is refused by the Model API in both lanes, and that is why no action in this job calls WfSvcOrder_GetSummary
reads the output of the node by the NAME of the node, not by the name of the action

actions.name: WfSvcOrder_MarkPaid
actions.description: Marca a encomenda como paga; Success=True se a encomenda existe

ops._why: the compact half: kind 'service' in the logic language also gives a ServiceAPIMethod -- Descriptor and CollectionDescriptor=ServiceActions equal to those of the hand-written half, and Public/Shareable are also born on. The get is a read, but the claim HAS a gate: this is the first of three ops that address the action by 'IServiceAction:WfSvcOrder_MarkPaid', and that path would not resolve if kind 'service' had produced an IServerAction

ops.name: WfSvcOrder_ControlNoConsumer
ops._why: THE CONTROL OF THE EXPERIMENT. It is not extra code: it is the half that was missing so that the central claim of the job can be falsified. A PRIVATE server action (the create is born private, no set of Public here) and without a single consumer, exactly the condition in which the two service actions of this job also are. Its UnusedUserAction is declared in expectedMessages, so if ODC stopped warning about unused server actions the job would fail with missingExpected -- and it is only because that side is mandatory that the silence on the OTHER side (the service actions, with no entry at all) means anything
the input is really consumed: an extra input would bring UnusedElement and swap the message that the control exists to prove

THIRD ACT starts with the baseline: the internal server action has exactly one consumer, the Summarize node inside the service action. It is because it has a consumer that it does not get UnusedUserAction -- and this has a gate: if the Action set of the Summarize had not settled, it would stay at zero and its UnusedUserAction is not declared

and it is the control, in the same run and on the same base, at zero consumers: the difference between it and the two service actions is only the TYPE, and that is why the message it receives and the ones they do not receive can be compared

the service action has ZERO and even so there is no new message at all about it. The number of this usages is not a gate (no Anvil verb checks a number); the gate is the message contract: with the control forcing UnusedUserAction to exist for unused server actions, the silence about this one can only come from ODC not giving it to service actions -- because their consumer is remote by definition. It is the structural proof of what the birth comment node says in words
the other one is also at zero, and also without a warning: it is not a fluke of the hand-written one

ops.value: Resumo de uma encomenda para consumidores remotos (contrato v2: sem RequestedBy)
ops._why: EDIT 1: swap text in an object that already exists, is already connected and has already been read. It is not configuration at birth -- it is the work that the coverage matrix said was missing
EDIT 2, and the surprise: with Public set to False, SHAREABLE falls along with it. They are the same decision seen from two sides -- a closed service action stops being shareable

and the other way around too: Public=True was set on the line above, but Shareable=False drags Public back to False. Shareable does not exist in SS11; it is the ODC property that decides whether the artifact crosses to another app

and this is the restoration: a single set puts both back to True. Four gets, four states of the pair -- and all four are READS, not proof, which this job says instead of hiding. The reason is not laziness, it is the arithmetic of the data contract: at the end it compares the LAST write of each property with what is there. If the job ended in a state produced by the drag (for example ending with 'set Shareable false' and letting Public fall on its own), the contract would read Public=False against the last write True and give 'Data property mismatch' -- that is, with today's verbs the coupling only shows up as a FAILURE of a correct job, never as proof of a green job. One verb is missing from the kernel; it is named in the last op of this file

DELETION 1: the input left over from the contract leaves an already-built action. brokenConsumers=0 and so it passes without force -- nobody read it. And it has gate (c), measured on this base: leaving it there gives 'Warning UnusedElement: Input Parameter RequestedBy is never used in Service Action WfSvcOrder_GetSummary'; since expectedMessages does not declare it, a deletion that did not settle would fail the job with unexpected

ops.name: OrderSummary
ops._why: EDIT 3, the one that counts: rename the OUTPUT of an already-written service action. The result brings consumers and expressionsRewritten, and what was rewritten was its own body

rename GATE, first direction: the output becomes addressable by the NEW name inside the service action. If the rename had not settled this path would not resolve and the job would return ok=False. Note the order required by the data contract: rename BEFORE, write values and expressions AFTER -- here nothing is written afterwards, only read

rename GATE, second direction, and it is the one that teaches: the internal server action HAS an output with the same old name, 'Summary'. If the rename were text search-and-replace, this output would have gone along and this path would stop resolving. It resolves, so the rename followed the key and not the text

the same on the inside: this assignment had 'Summary' on BOTH sides. The Variable was the output of the service action and became OrderSummary by itself; the Value is still Summarize.Summary because that Summary is the output of the SERVER action. The detail is visible here, but what pins it down are the two gets above and the Verify (a broken expression would give a new error and isValid=False)
the other service action was also born with the OutSystems ICommentNode, even though it was created by the compact language
DELETION 2: delete the child that the PLATFORM puts at birth. It is done in only one of the two so that the final dump shows the two forms side by side

THE ONLY WRITE OF THE PAIR THAT THE CONTRACT CAN PIN DOWN, and it stays like this on purpose until the end of the job. The birth of an IServiceAction is Public=True/Shareable=True; a job that ends in that state cannot tell 'I wrote True' from 'I never touched', and that was the gap the checker caught in the four gets above. Ending here at Public=False, the data contract now requires at the end a value that birth did not give -- if the set had not settled, 'Data property mismatch' would come out with expected false and actual true
and the read shows the drag here too: Shareable fell to False without anyone writing to it. This number is a read, not a gate; the Public=False next to it is the gate

and it stays at zero consumers ALREADY PRIVATE -- and even so without UnusedUserAction, while WfSvcOrder_ControlNoConsumer, private and at zero in the same run, has to receive it. It is the tightest form of the contrast: same visibility, same number of consumers, different types, different messages
final read of the edited service action: Description v2, Public and Shareable at True again, InputParameters back to 1

the whole flow read back: the birth comment that remained, the Summarize calling the private server action, the If on the output of the node, the assign to the renamed output and the raise of the user exception
and the compact one without the comment, with the get/if/assign/save that the language generated
the user exception is raised in the False branch of the If

ops.name: WfSvcOrder_GetSummary
ops._why: CLOSING, and the account of what remained unproven. Three claims of this job remain without a gate and none of them is resolved by writing more ops: (1) the TEXT of the birth ICommentNode -- the existence has a gate, the words do not; (2) the four states of the Public/Shareable pair in WfSvcOrder_GetSummary; (3) the numbers of the usages. The three are of the same family: they are values that the job READS and does not WRITE, and the kernel only knows how to verify what was written (DataAssertions.RememberValue keeps the last write by key and CheckDataContract compares it at the end; the verbs are create/set/link/move/reference/usages/rename/duplicate/delete/get/find/replace/layout/spec/logic/screen/html/dump, and none of them verifies). KERNEL CHANGE REQUESTED, the smallest one that resolves the three: a verified-read verb, {"op":"expect","target":"<ref>","prop":"<Property>","value":<expected>}, that reads the property the way the get already reads it and adds the divergence to the same list of dataContract.differences, coming out with the same 'Data property mismatch: ...' line that already exists in JobRunner.cs. With it, 'Shareable=False drags Public to False' becomes an op that fails the job if ODC changes its mind, instead of a sentence in a _why. As long as that verb does not exist, the rule of this lane is the one that this file follows: a claim without a gate says it has no gate. And the fourth claim, the refusal of the local call, does not fit in a green job at all -- its place is a tests/jobs-odc-negative with expectError on 'A OutSystems.Model.Logic.IServiceAction cannot be used as the value for the OutSystems.Model.Logic.Nodes.IExecuteServerActionNode.Action property in a OutSystems.Model.Logic.IServerAction', which this job does not create because it can only touch itself
